sections.section_name: Section A - Objective Type / MCQs / True-False

questions.question_text: In the context of evaluating an AI model, which term describes the scenario where the model incorrectly predicts the positive class?
Which Natural Language Processing (NLP) technique represents text as a collection of words, completely ignoring grammar and word order but keeping track of frequency?
What is the primary function of the Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) algorithm in NLP?
options: A) To translate text from one language to another
B) To evaluate the importance of a word to a document in a corpus
C) To convert speech into text data
D) To check grammatical errors in a sentence
questions.answer: B) To evaluate the importance of a word to a document in a corpus

questions.question_text: True or False: In Computer Vision, 'Segmentation' refers to the process of dividing an image into multiple segments or pixels to simplify and change the representation of an image into something more meaningful.
Which metric provides the percentage of true positive predictions among all the positive predictions made by the model?
In a Confusion Matrix, what does 'True Negative' (TN) represent?
options: A) The model predicted Yes, and the actual value was No
B) The model predicted No, and the actual value was No
C) The model predicted Yes, and the actual value was Yes
D) The model predicted No, and the actual value was Yes
questions.answer: B) The model predicted No, and the actual value was No

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental task in Computer Vision?
True or False: 'Stemming' is an NLP text normalization step that always results in a valid dictionary word.
Which evaluation metric is the harmonic mean of Precision and Recall, providing a balance between the two?
In object tracking pipelines, what is the primary goal?
options: A) To identify static objects in a single image
B) To estimate the trajectory of a moving object over time in a video sequence
C) To enhance the resolution of a blurry image
D) To convert a color image into grayscale
questions.answer: B) To estimate the trajectory of a moving object over time in a video sequence

questions.question_text: Define 'Lemmatization' in the context of text normalization. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Lemmatization reduces words to their meaningful base or dictionary form (lemma) by analyzing vocabulary and morphological structure, unlike stemming which just chops off affixes.

questions.question_text: What is the specific purpose of an 'Object Detection' algorithm in Computer Vision? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Object detection goes beyond classification by not only identifying what objects are in an image but also locating them precisely using bounding boxes.

questions.question_text: Explain what a 'False Negative' signifies in a medical diagnostic AI system. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A False Negative means the AI incorrectly predicts a patient is healthy (Negative) when they actually have the disease (True), potentially delaying critical treatment.

questions.question_text: Briefly describe the 'Bag of Words' (BoW) model in Natural Language Processing. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: BoW is a text representation technique describing the occurrence of words within a document. It creates a vocabulary and counts word frequencies, ignoring grammar and order.

questions.question_text: Why is the F1 Score often a better metric than Accuracy when dealing with imbalanced datasets? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Accuracy can be misleading in imbalanced datasets if the model just predicts the majority class. The F1 Score balances Precision and Recall, providing a more reliable performance measure.

sections.section_name: Section C - Short Answer Application Problems

questions.question_text: A tech company builds a spam filter. In a test run of 100 emails, it correctly identified 20 spam emails (TP) and 70 legitimate emails (TN). It incorrectly marked 5 legitimate emails as spam (FP) and missed 5 spam emails (FN). Construct the Confusion Matrix layout for this scenario. [30-40 words]
questions.answer:
The Confusion Matrix layout is: 
True Positives (TP) = 20 (Actual Spam, Predicted Spam)
False Positives (FP) = 5 (Actual Legitimate, Predicted Spam)
False Negatives (FN) = 5 (Actual Spam, Predicted Legitimate)
True Negatives (TN) = 70 (Actual Legitimate, Predicted Legitimate)

questions.question_text: Outline the necessary text normalization steps an NLP pipeline must perform on the sentence 'The quick brown foxes are running fast!' before applying a TF-IDF algorithm. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The pipeline should perform lowercase conversion ('the quick brown foxes are running fast!'), remove punctuation ('the quick brown foxes are running fast'), remove stop words ('quick brown foxes running fast'), and apply lemmatization ('quick brown fox run fast').

sections.section_name: Section D - Long Answer / Case-Based Technical Scenarios

questions.question_text: Read the following case context: A city deploys a Computer Vision system for automated traffic monitoring to track vehicle speeds and segment different vehicle types (cars, buses, bikes) at a busy intersection. Detail the specific computer vision pipelines required for this task, explaining how pixel segmentation and object tracking collaborate to achieve the desired outcome. [50-70 words]
questions.answer: The system first requires Instance Segmentation to analyze pixels and accurately separate different vehicle types from the background and each other, classifying them as cars, buses, or bikes. Then, an Object Tracking pipeline assigns a unique ID to each segmented vehicle, following its trajectory across consecutive video frames over time. By calculating the distance traveled across pixels between frames, the system can estimate vehicle speeds.

questions.question_text: Read the following case context: An AI model predicting fraudulent bank transactions yields the following results: TP = 40, FP = 10, FN = 20, TN = 930. Compute the Precision, Recall, and Accuracy metrics. Based on these numbers, analyze why Accuracy might present a misleading view of the model's effectiveness in stopping fraud. [50-70 words]
questions.answer: Accuracy is (40+930)/1000 = 97%. Precision is TP/(TP+FP) = 40/50 = 80%. Recall is TP/(TP+FN) = 40/60 = 66.6%. While 97% Accuracy seems excellent, it is misleading due to the massive number of True Negatives (normal transactions). The Recall of 66.6% shows the model actually misses a third of all fraudulent transactions (False Negatives), making it less effective for security purposes than the Accuracy suggests.
